newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares end strongly, assisted by bonds, bills.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares end strongly, assisted by bonds, bills.

text.p: * NZ shares end strongly while interest rates ease
* Market defies pre-election nerves
* Overseas investor interest continues unabated
Price movements at close.
LAST CHG

The New Zealand share market's pre-election rally continued unabated on Thursday with overseas investors still seemingly undaunted by the prospect of a left leaning administration after the October 12 poll.
"I can't get over the strength of all our markets with the polls pointing towards the likelihood of a left-slanting coalition," Tim Snedden at ANZ Securities said.
"To me the markets seem to be pricing in very much a right wing coalition, which is not what the polls are suggesting right now," he said.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index closed 14.36 points up at 2,235.73 on respectable turnover worth NZ$69 million.
Stronger overseas markets and strength in the domestic bond market was underpinning the local equities market, brokers said.
There was continued offshore investment, although concentrated in just a few of the leaders and some special second line stocks.
Brierley Investments ended steady at $1.37 but was still struggling after the disappointing price set for the British float of Thistle hotels.
Fletcher Building was particularly strong, gaining 11 cents to $3.43, as was Telecom, up six at $6.95.
Outside the leaders, Kiwi Income attracted high turnover, indicating some repositioning by local and international funds before the upcoming convertible note and cash issue.
Newly listed TransAlta NZ continued its meteoric rise, gaining 15 to $1.90, driven mostly by private clients, although a large line of 500,000 shares was transacted at $1.80 a share.
